description_en: Twośikharatemples from the 13th-15th century.The monuments are found in the middle of terraced fields, at a hundred meters to the north of the Kālī Bazar area in Rāvatakoṭa. In Kālī Bazar is a group of five temples (DLK0280) that can be situated around the 14th-15th century (Andolfatto 2019;Sharma 2012, p. 112-115).Twośikharatemples are facing one another. Temple 001, is oriented to the north, while temple 002 is oriented to the south. The architecture of the monuments follows the same rules as other śikhara built in west Nepal between the 13th and the 15th century. Of limited size, they may have been built to honor the memory of ancestors or a lineage. The religious affiliation of the temples is yet impossible to establish. Only the lintel of temple 002 contains a carved decoration in the form of a rosette on the lintel.The roofs would usually be topped by one or twoāmalakarings. There are currently none at the site.In West Nepalśikharatemples are known asdevala. Hence the termduidevalafor a pair ofśikharatemples.
monument_assessment: Other, Heavily damaged (collapsed, demolished, major cracks and structural damages), Structural damages
references: REFERENCES Andolfatto, David C. Le Pays aux Cent-Vingt-Cinq-Mille Montagnes. Etude Archéologique du Bassin de la Karnali (Népal) entre le XIIe et le XVIe siècle . Paris: Sorbonne University, 2019. Sharma, Dilli Raj. Heritage of Western Nepal. Art and Architecture . Kathmandu: Centre for Nepal and Asian Studies, 2012.
